label: Critique the units
description: Do the units cover the behaviour, and do the invariants say anything? (feature.md §4).

target_id.description: The deliverable, flow, component or unit id this is about.

disposition.description: fixed: this pass changed to answer it. rejected: the finding is wrong, and `note` says why. blocked: this pass cannot see how to make progress on it — `note` says what it would need.

note.description: What changed, why the finding is wrong, or what is missing. Required for rejected and blocked.

operation.user:
Judge this design. Two questions: **do the units cover the behaviour, and do the
invariants say anything?**

Structure is already machine-checked. Spend your attention on substance.

## The units and their docs

{{.inputs.units}}

{{.inputs.unit_docs}}

_Paths — open them with `read_file`._

## The contracts

{{.inputs.contract_docs}}

## The decision records

{{.inputs.decisions}}

## What they have to serve

{{.inputs.components}}

{{.inputs.flows}}

## The docs this phase reads

{{.inputs.working_set}}

**These are paths, not contents.** Open each one with `read_file` before you start. Read the
file as it is now — an earlier state in this phase may have edited it since the run began.

## Findings from the previous pass

{{.inputs.prior_findings}}

Each carries the author's own `disposition` — what it says it did:

- `fixed` — check it. A finding recorded as fixed that is not fixed is worse than one
  never addressed, and it is why this list is here rather than in your memory.
- `rejected` — the author says the finding was wrong. It may be right. Read the `note`
  and let it go if it holds; restating a finding already answered is how a loop spends
  four passes going nowhere.
- `blocked` — the author cannot see how to make progress. Decide whether that is true.
  If it is, raise `target: 'ask'` and stop: nothing downstream of you can supply it.

A finding that comes back unchanged twice is a finding about the author state, not the
work.

## What to check

- **Components and flows with no unit behind them** — and units that serve
  nothing.
- **Invariants that cannot be false.** "The store returns valid data" is
  decoration. One worth writing names a state the system could actually reach and
  is forbidden from, and phase 5 has to be able to assert it. Take each invariant
  and try to write the failing test in your head; where you cannot, say so.
- **Failure modes that are only the easy ones.** Which has it *not* answered: two
  writers at once, a process killed mid-write, a partial read, a retry that
  duplicates, a clock that moved? Naming "network error" and stopping is the
  usual shape of an incomplete list.
- **Every failure mode maps to a UX state.** If one has none, that is `blocked`:
  either phase 2 missed a state or the failure cannot occur, and a person
  decides which.
- **One owner per fact.** Where two stores hold the same thing, is the source of
  truth named and the other one derived?
- **Units that are one responsibility split across a file boundary**, or one file
  holding two responsibilities.
- **Is the compatibility answer honest about existing data** — not just the
  schema, but rows written by the version running right now?
- **Budgets that are adjectives.** If nothing is at risk, say so and drop the
  section.
- An architecture change lives in `architecture.md`, not only in the unit doc.

## What to produce

`findings` (severity · claim · evidence · target_id), `max_severity`,
`max_severity_rank`, and `target` — `draft`, `explore`, or `upstream` where the
component or the flow is what is wrong.

There is a fourth `target`, `ask` — neither you nor the author can see how to make
progress: what is missing is a measurement nobody has taken, a decision only a person can
make, or a fact that is not in the repo. A person always sees this one, and it leaves the
loop AT ONCE rather than spending the passes that remain. Raise it the pass you know, not
the pass you run out — being stuck on pass 1 is not improved by two more passes of the
same. The author's `blocked` dispositions are where to look first; judge them rather than
taking them at their word.

evidence.description: A path:line, a quotation, or a reproduction.

target_id.description: The deliverable, flow, component or unit id this is about.

inputs.unit_docs.description: Path to unit_docs. Read it with read_file — the file as it is now, not a copy taken at state entry.

inputs.severity_threshold.description: Substantial means at or above this.

inputs.architecture_amendment.description: The amendment this pass submits against a standing doc, when it submits one. It travels beside the deliverables rather than inside them, so judge it as its own claim — and do not report it missing when it is present here.

inputs.prior_findings.description: The previous pass's findings AND what the author did with each, so the loop converges instead of rediscovering the same weakness. A `blocked` disposition is the author saying it cannot see how to make progress — judge it, and raise `target: 'ask'` where it is right.

inputs.working_set.description: Paths to the docs this phase reads — its standing docs and the catalog entries that bear on the feature. Open them with read_file: the file as it is now, not a copy taken before this phase started editing.
